title: QVC: Living Large With First West Coast Distribution Center
summary: QVC has opened its first West Coast distribution center in Ontario, California, a 1 million-square-foot facility expected to handle over 20% of its total shipments and employ 1,000 people by 2020. This move aims to improve delivery speed to West Coast customers and accommodate the evolving retail landscape, despite increasing competition from e-commerce giants like Amazon and challenges posed by changing consumer demographics and social media. The article also highlights QVC's financial performance, noting an 11% increase in American e-commerce revenue and a 2% increase in U.S. total revenue in Q2 2016, while acknowledging a recent deceleration in demand.

title: Lands’ End to Start Selling Items on Amazon.com
summary: Lands’ End Inc. announced its plan to begin selling select merchandise on Amazon.com Inc. by the end of the month. This move comes as the struggling apparel maker seeks to expand its reach to consumers and tap into the e-commerce giant's rapid growth. The items will include products from its Lands’ End sports, footwear, and Canvas collections.

title: Counterfeiting Causes 750,000 Job Losses, eBay and Amazon Main Culprits (eBay Comments Added)
summary: A report by The Counterfeit Report indicates that the sale of fake products on platforms like Amazon and eBay is a $1.7 trillion global criminal enterprise, destroying 750,000 U.S. jobs and costing U.S. businesses over $250 billion annually. The report criticizes both Amazon and eBay for their handling of counterfeit items, alleging difficulties in identification and problematic refund processes. eBay, in response, asserts its commitment to combating counterfeit goods through various programs and technologies, and highlights a legal victory against Mr. Crosby of The Counterfeit Report.

title: Operation license for Amazon’s Belo Monte mega-dam suspended
summary: A Brazilian judge has suspended the operating license for the controversial Belo Monte dam in the Amazon due to the operator's failure to fulfill a key compensation commitment. The Norte Energia consortium did not complete the agreed-upon drinking water and sewage systems for Altamira, a condition for building and running the dam. This failure has led to environmental concerns, including sewage polluting the Xingu River and potential groundwater contamination in Altamira.

title: Do Tech Companies Know What It Takes To Make A Car?
authors: ['Alex Webb', 'Elisabeth Behrmann and Gerrit De Vynck']
summary: Magna International Inc., the world's largest contract manufacturer of cars, is positioning itself to build vehicles for Silicon Valley tech companies like Apple, Google, and Uber. While tech companies have expertise in software, they lack the experience in manufacturing complex vehicles, making partners like Magna essential. Magna expects this new demand to significantly boost its revenue from contract manufacturing, with a focus on autonomous and electric vehicles.

title: Will Lands’ End sink or swim on Amazon?
summary: Lands' End is partnering with Amazon to sell select apparel, a move that retail experts are debating for its potential risks and rewards. While Amazon offers vast reach, some fear it could lead to the demise of brands unable to control pricing and promotion effectively. This decision comes as Lands' End tries to update its image and boost e-commerce sales after spinning off from Sears.

title: Analytics in the driver’s seat at Ford
summary: This article highlights how Ford Motor Co. is integrating analytics into all aspects of its business, led by Chief Data and Analytics Officer Paul Ballew. It discusses Ford's use of analytics for both core business functions and emerging areas like connected vehicles, smart mobility, and autonomous driving. The piece also covers Ford's approach to an analytics culture, talent development, and the importance of open-source tools and cognitive computing.

title: Oracle Head Larry Ellison Talks A Big Game Against Amazon Web Services
summary: Oracle's executive chairman, Larry Ellison, declared Amazon Web Services as Oracle's primary competitor in cloud computing during the company's annual customer conference. Despite Amazon's leading position and significantly higher IaaS revenue, Ellison emphasized Oracle's advancements like Cloud@Customer and aimed to undercut Amazon on pricing, while also discussing Oracle's entry into AI technologies.

title: Amazon isn’t just online — it’s opening a real bookstore in Dedham
summary: Amazon is expanding its physical retail presence by opening a brick-and-mortar bookstore in Dedham, Massachusetts, at the Legacy Place mall in 2017. This new location will join existing Amazon Books stores in Seattle and San Diego, and planned stores in Portland, Chicago, and New York. The bookstores serve as a hybrid model, offering highly-rated books, Amazon's electronic devices, and a "Trojan horse" strategy to promote devices and allow for serendipitous browsing.

title: Why Tech Data Dropped $2.6 Billion to Buy Avnet’s Technology Services Unit
summary: Tech Data is acquiring Avnet's Technology Services business for $2.6 billion, a move that highlights the ongoing consolidation within the technology distribution industry. This deal will strengthen Tech Data's presence in Asia and its data center offerings, while the broader trend of cloud computing is impacting traditional hardware vendors and distributors. The acquisition aims to enable Tech Data to better compete in a changing market where corporate computing is shifting to public cloud providers.

title: Etsy snares AI startup Blackbird Technologies
summary: Etsy has acquired AI startup Blackbird Technologies to enhance its site search and product recommendation capabilities using machine learning, natural language processing, and image recognition. The full Blackbird team, including co-founders Nikhil Raghavan and Manju Rajashekar, has joined Etsy. This acquisition is seen as a strategic move to help Etsy stay competitive, especially against Amazon's Handmade store, and improve customer experience.

title: Why These Tech Companies Keep Running Thousands Of Failed Experiments
summary: Innovative companies like Amazon, Google, and Netflix succeed by running thousands of experiments, recognizing that most will fail but the few big wins will yield massive returns. These companies reduce the cost of experimentation and empower employees to test ideas, leading to significant innovations and market share growth. The article highlights how this approach resolves tensions between creative teams and executives by relying on data-driven decisions rather than mere approvals.

title: Govt. finalizes cloud service providers; AWS name missing
summary: The Indian government has provisionally empaneled several Cloud Service Providers (CSPs) for its 'MeghRaj' GI Cloud initiative, with notable companies like Microsoft and IBM making the list. However, Amazon Web Services (AWS) is conspicuously absent from the finalized list of providers. This empanelment aims to offer a new model of cloud computing services to government departments across India.

title: Amazon is indeed coming to Dedham
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has confirmed its plans to open a physical bookstore in Dedham, Massachusetts, in 2017, expanding its brick-and-mortar retail experiments. The store will be located at the Legacy Place mall and will offer a mix of books and Amazon's consumer electronics like Kindle and Echo devices. This move follows the opening of similar bookstores in Seattle and San Diego, with additional locations planned for Portland, Ore., and Chicago.

title: Oracle’s Larry Ellison has a new target: Amazon
summary: Oracle’s co-founder Larry Ellison has set his sights on Amazon as the new primary rival, focusing on the cloud computing arena. During the OpenWorld user conference, Oracle announced product upgrades and highlighted its growth strategy in cloud computing. The company is positioning itself against Amazon Web Services, currently the leader in cloud infrastructure.

title: Private labels a tool in battle with Amazon
summary: Retailers like Canadian Tire, Hudson's Bay, Loblaw, and Wal-Mart Canada are increasingly focusing on private labels and exclusive products to combat online competition from Amazon. These private brands help prevent price-matching, potentially offer higher profit margins, and create a unique appeal for customers. Canadian Tire is even considering selling its private label lines internationally, potentially through Amazon, as a competitive tool.

title: Adobe partners with Microsoft to use Azure as ‘preferred solution’ for cloud services
summary: Adobe and Microsoft have announced a strategic cloud partnership, making Microsoft Azure the "preferred cloud platform" for Adobe Marketing Cloud, Adobe Creative Cloud, and Adobe Document Cloud. This alliance positions Adobe Marketing Cloud as the "preferred marketing service" for Microsoft Dynamics 365, intensifying competition with Salesforce, IBM, and Oracle in customer relationship management and marketing technologies. Both companies emphasize data integration to create new sales and marketing capabilities, though the "preferred" deals are not exclusive.

title: Apple, Inc. Sold Over $2.5 Billion Worth of Apple Watches in 2015
summary: In 2015, Apple sold over $2.5 billion worth of Apple Watches, positioning the company as the world's No. 2 watchmaker by revenue, despite the product only shipping in volume for half the year. The article estimates Apple Watch revenue to be between $2.5 billion and $4.5 billion, and with an estimated average selling price of $500, this suggests 5 million to 9 million units sold in 2015. This makes Apple a significant competitor in the watch market, surpassing publicly traded Fossil.
